messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer report: private deployment hitting 502s talking to svc.payments.internal from their VPC. They say the name resolves to a public IP instead of the private ENI. Seen this pattern before?

priya: ugh split-horizon. can you paste a dig from inside their VPC?

alex: pasted from their repro VM:```
$ dig svc.payments.internal +short
54.23.11.2
$ dig svc.payments.internal @169.254.169.253 +short
54.23.11.2
```expected: 10.0.5.12 (private endpoint).

support-bot: Note: customer environment = us-east-1, Private deployment vpc-0a1b2c3d, resolver rules: outbound to 10.0.1.5, no conditional forwarders reported. Config ID: CUST-4891.

dan: if dig against VPC resolver is returning public IP then either private hosted zone not associated or there is a public hosted zone with the same name higher priority. run: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name svc.payments.internal` and `aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations`

alex: they ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name svc.payments.internal` and got:```
HostedZones:
- Id: /hostedzone/Z3PUBLIC12345
  Name: svc.payments.internal.
- Id: /hostedzone/Z2PRIVATE67890
  Name: svc.payments.internal.
```they also showed that only the public zone is associated with the customer account's VPC (weird).

priya: that's the smoking gun. if both zones exist, the private zone must be associated with the VPC that does the resolution. maybe it was created in another account/tenant. Ask them to check VPC associations for the private hosted zone id Z2PRIVATE67890.

alex: they checked Z2PRIVATE67890 and saw associations: `[]` (no associations). Private zone exists but not attached to their VPC. they said it used to be associated until a Terraform change last week.

james: possible race during infra change. Two remediation options: associate the private hosted zone with their VPC, or delete/migrate the public hosted zone entry to avoid name collision. need to coordinate change window.

emily: small gotcha — even if you associate the private zone, any Resolver rules that forward to a remote IP may still prefer external answers if the resolver behavior was changed. ask them to run `dig +trace svc.payments.internal` to confirm where resolution stops.

alex: they ran `dig +trace`:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace svc.payments.internal
;; global options: +cmd
.  518400 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
...
svc.payments.internal. 60 IN A 54.23.11.2
```trace ended at public zone.

dan: yep public zone is winning. Also check Route53 cross-account delegation: private zone could be in another account and not associated. If that is by design, we need to update docs and enforce checks in our onboarding playbook.

priya: for immediate customer fix: request permission to associate Z2PRIVATE67890 -> vpc-0a1b2c3d. If they can't, they can remove the public record from the public zone or move private zone into their account.

alex: customer asked if this could cause TLS issues — they keep seeing TLS handshake failures after they pinned routing to public IP in a rush. any thoughts?

james: yes. connecting to the public IP hits our external load balancer with certs for `api.redwood.com`, while the client expects `svc.payments.internal` (SNI mismatch). That will cause TLS errors. rolling back to private IP should fix TLS. Also envoy mTLS policies might reject the external connection.

emily: also check security groups/firewall — if they associated private zone but the ENI IP is blocked in their NACLs or SGs, connection will still fail with timeouts. recommend a connectivity test: `curl -v --resolve svc.payments.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://svc.payments.internal/health` from their VM inside the VPC to confirm TLS and SG.

alex: customer ran `curl` after we guided them (once associated) and got:```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://svc.payments.internal/health
*   Trying 10.0.5.12...
* Connected to svc.payments.internal (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

priya: handshake failure — get server-side logs for TLS: are we terminating TLS at LB or at service? If LB, check SNI and certs. If service, check allowed cipher suites and client cert expectations.

alex: customer says we terminate TLS at their private endpoint (they manage certs). they recently rotated certs via ACM and might have misconfigured SANs.

james: ask for `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername svc.payments.internal -showcerts` output and the server cert CN/SAN.

alex: they provided the s_client output and cert shows CN=internal-payments, SANs: `internal-payments.local` only (missing `svc.payments.internal`). No wonder.

emily: action items summarized: 1) associate private hosted zone Z2PRIVATE67890 -> customer VPC (or remove public record) 2) verify resolver rules and forwarders 3) validate SG/NACL egress rules allow 10.0.5.12:443 4) fix cert SAN to include svc.payments.internal 5) rollback any emergency route updates that pointed to public IP.

priya: I'm going to attach this to CUST-4891-escalation and request DBA/infra to approve the VPC association. tagging infra for coordination.

support-bot: Escalation created: CUST-4891-ESCL. Assigned to infra oncall. ETA for initial contact: 30m.

dan: also adding a preventive doc note: when doing infra as code changes, add a `route53:verify_vpc_associations` post-run check to CI to catch accidental disassociation.

alex: customer confirmed after association + cert fix they can curl OK and 502s disappeared. closing loop and sending postmortem checklist. :tada:

priya: nice — please add remediation steps to the support KB so next time we can triage faster.

alex: will do. thanks all.
